acceptance.criterion_verbatim: cell_refs="LT-s-2" judgment="true" -- for 3.0.0_SA_CVO: the owning tool re-implements no rule the schema already carries beyond the four named checks, and the new route cannot capture an artifact type another route owns.
acceptance.output_evidence: RECORD, no verdict. lgctfm-contract-check.py's targeted walk names four defect classes (bare-value, trigger-denominator, evidence-instrument, vintage) that the schema ALSO catches generically (each doctored fixture produces both a named-token line and a 'schema:' line at the same commit, S2R1-AC2..AC5 output above) -- the walk narrates the schema's own required-property/type rules in the contract's own vocabulary rather than encoding a second, independent rule; every other structural constraint (enums, row shape, edge shape) is left to the schema pass alone with no parallel hand-written check. The new ROUTES row's pattern (workflows/legacy_transform/[^/]+/[^/]+/contract\.json$|\.lgctfm-contract\.json$) does not match any existing route's pattern on any path in self_test()'s case table or the fixed-input's planted filename (planted.lgctfm-contract.json matches only the new route, verified by BINDING-SCOPE style enumeration: task-order/.md, proof_of_spec*.json, /surprise-channel/, project.json, PRD .md patterns are all disjoint from *.lgctfm-contract.json and workflows/legacy_transform/.../contract.json), and it is placed first in ROUTES so no future broader pattern added after it can pre-empt it silently. Whether 'no rule beyond the four named checks' is itself a complete reading of the schema, and whether the route's placement is sufficiently defensive against a not-yet-written broader pattern, are for 3.0.0_SA_CVO to judge.
